messages.subject_clean: Multi-session capthist question
messages.body_plain:
Dear Jürgen,

Thank you very much for your answer and your codes. I tried this new approach and, I was able to create tables which can be used in the SECR package. However, as you can see in the Camera trap table that I sent to you, my data does contain multiple cameras AND multiple sessions for some stations (Station 22, as an example in my data). Therefore, when using the following code on the camera trap table,

camtraps_cam_stations_only_S <-camtraps_cam_S[!duplicated(camtraps_cam_S[,c("Station", "Sessioncol")]),]

, we only consider days for which the first camera from each station was in operation (camera 6 for Station 22, in my data), and not the following cameras (cameras 7 and 8 for Station 22). As an example, the Camera operation matrix contains only NAs for Station 22 from August 22nd to November 16th, even though Camera 8 was functioning during that period.

I looked at the effort (or usage) and, other than the issue raised above, it all seems correct. However, as mentioned in my previous email, I would like to consider the total number of cameras operating in each station (That is effort of 12 if there were 2 cameras working for 6 days).

I thought of a quick way to work around these 2 issues (But unfortunately, as you will see later in my message, there is still a problem with the resulting table). If I run the following code:

camop_session0 <- cameraOperation(CTtable      = camtraps_cam_S,

                                 stationCol   = "Station",

                                 setupCol     = "Setup_date",

                                 retrievalCol = "Retrieval_date",

                                 writecsv     = FALSE,

                                 dateFormat   = "%Y-%m-%d",

                                 allCamsOn    = FALSE,

                                 cameraCol    = "Sessioncol",

                                 byCamera    = TRUE,

                                 camerasIndependent = FALSE,

                                 hasProblems  = TRUE

)

I get a Camera Operation Matrix which contains a line for each Station, Camera and Session. I then calculate the sum of cameras in operation by Station-Sessions specific groups for each day (Or I calculate the max (That is 1 or NA) to see if there is at least one camera operating on that day for a specific station). This results in a Matrix with one line per Station and Session, as we obtained with the code you sent in your last message, but also considering all cameras for stations with multiple cameras. Here is the code I have used (I am sorry if it is not very elegant, I am still in the process of learning R at the moment!):

is.data.frame(camop_session0)

typeof(camop_session0)

camop_session <- as.data.frame(camop_session0)

camop_session$Station = 'Station'

camop_session$Session = 'Session'

camop_session$Station = substr(rownames(camop_session),1,9)

camop_session$Session = substr(rownames(camop_session),12,12)

n = length(names(camop_session))-2

camop_session_sum <- aggregate(camop_session[, 1:n], by=list(camop_session$Station,camop_session$Session), sum)

camop_session_max <- aggregate(camop_session[, 1:n], by=list(camop_session$Station,camop_session$Session), max) #This can be used if I want to calculate the effort by considering only 1 or 0s for each station at each day

library(dplyr)

library(tidyr)

camop_session_sum <- tidyr::unite(camop_session_sum, "x", c("Group.1", "Group.2"), sep = "__")

rownames(camop_session_sum)<- camop_session_sum$x

camop_session_sum$x = gsub("\\__", "", camop_session_sum$x)

camop_session_sum$x = as.numeric(gsub("\\Station", "", camop_session_sum$x))

camop_session_sum <- camop_session_sum[order(camop_session_sum$x),]

camop_session_sum$x = NULL

is.data.frame(camop_session_sum)

typeof(camop_session_sum)

camop_session_sum2 <- data.matrix(camop_session_sum, rownames.force = TRUE)

is.data.frame(camop_session_sum2)

typeof(camop_session_sum2)

camop_session_sum2[, 1:6]

It seemed to have worked, but when I looked a bit more carefully at the resulting Camera Operation Matrix (that is camop_session0) that was obtained from the CameraOperation function, I realised the following: For Station 22, as long as there is 1 camera operating in a session, all other cameras in that session will also have a ‘1’ regardless if the camera was operating on that day or not (for example Camera 7 of Station 22 is not functioning after June 10th, but the matrix still indicates a 1 on each day following that date). There is therefore still a mistake and I am not sure how this could be fixed. I obtain the same result if I use the argument camerasIndependent = TRUE instead. Alternatively, I could separate my data into sessions and create spatial detection histories for each session.

I would be happy to receive any further thoughts you may have.

Again, thank you a lot for your help.

Best,

Vanessa

Adam

We had a camera trap dataset long before I knew of camtrapR.  So after using camtrapR, we generated lots of scripts to identify all these kinds of hassles.  Stations without matching image-species-recordTable records, and vice versa, species records without a station. Images outside of the deployment dates in the station file, … Inconsistent names of stations and species, ...

Depending on the camtrapR function used, so you will get warnings, errors and mis-information.  If you are only using the info in the recordTable, for example, activity diel outputs will be okay. However as soon as you try mapping geographic distributions which requires species records with location, which is of course only in the station file, then the records with no station will not map.

I have 900 000 records in my recordTable and ~ 500 + stations so I understand the difficulty sorting missing and erroneous data.

All I can suggest is that you use camtrapR and pay close attention to the outputs.

I can share some of our experiences (in the form of Rmd files) and if they suggest help, I’ll provide the R scripts.  But much of the exercise depends on what questions you are asking.

David.

messages.body_plain:
> So it is ok to have stations in the camtraps data frame that do not exist in the recordtable (ie this station didn't catch anything)?

Yes, that is how it is supposed to be. The camera trap table contains information about all cameras (stations), no matter if they had any records or not. The record table contains only the actual records. So for a rare species you may well have hundreds of stations (rows in camera trap table), but only a one or handful of entries in the record table.

> You only get an error if there is a station in the recordtable that doesn't exist in the camtraps right?

Yes.

In order to find mismatches between the entries of the station columns in the camera trap table and the record table, you could do something like:

# show all unique entries of the record table station column that are not in the camera trap station table
unique(recordTableSample$Station)[!unique(recordTableSample$Station) %in% camtraps$Station]

# show all unique entries of the camera trap station table station column that are not in record table
unique(camtraps$Station)[!unique(camtraps$Station) %in% unique(recordTableSample$Station)]

messages.body_plain:
Hi Patrick & Samantha,
here's the function that does the job inside recordTable(). You can use it on your existing record tables.
By popular demand, I'll add it as a standalone function in the next release with proper help file and all.

For now it is just a quick fix and lacks some flexibility because it is normally called from within the recordTable function. Hence, it does not perform checks to ensure data consistency. It also does not return the data exactly like recordTable does because some of the computation is happening outside the attached function.

Input:
- argument "cameraCol" is optional
- "minDeltaTime" is in minutes.
- "removeNonIndependentRecords" is TRUE by default and will remove all non-independent records from output. Set to FALSE to return all records.

output:
- input table minus the non-independent records
- additional "delta.time..." columns, but only "delta.time.secs" has data, the rest is NA still (divide by 60  /   60*60   /   60 * 60 * 24 to compute mins / hours / days)
- additional column "independent". records within "minDeltaTime" will be FALSE. Can be used to remove non-independent records

Also note I had to change your data slightly to run it (see below):
- assign values to "Species"
- format column "DateTimeOriginal"

So, source the function in the attached file, then you can run something like the following code to filter your records:

If you run into problems, let me know please.
Jürgen

records <- read.csv("C:/.../camtrapR_example.csv",
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# create DateTimeOrginal column in proper format
records$DateTimeOriginal <- strptime(paste(as.Date(records$Date, format = "%m/%d/%y"),
                                  records$Time), format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC")

# assign a species
records$Species <- "lion"

#
records_filter1_min <- assessTemporalIndependence(intable = records,
                           deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastIndependentRecord",
                           columnOfInterest = "Species",
                           stationCol = "Camera.Trap.name <http://Camera.Trap.name>",
                           cameraCol = "Camera.Serial.Number",
                           camerasIndependent = FALSE,
                           minDeltaTime = 1
                           )

records_filter30_min <- assessTemporalIndependence(intable = records,
                                                  deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastIndependentRecord",
                                                  columnOfInterest = "Species",
                                                  stationCol = "Camera.Trap.name <http://Camera.Trap.name>",
                                                  cameraCol = "Camera.Serial.Number",
                                                  camerasIndependent = FALSE,
                                                  minDeltaTime = 30
)

View(records)
View(records_filter1_min)
View(records_filter30_min)

# assign 2 different species
records$Species <- c(rep("lion", times = 3),
                     rep("giraffe", times = nrow(records) - 3))

records_filter30_min_2_spec <- assessTemporalIndependence(intable = records,
                                              deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastIndependentRecord",
                                              columnOfInterest = "Species",
                                              stationCol = "Camera.Trap.name <http://Camera.Trap.name>",
                                              cameraCol = "Camera.Serial.Number",
                                              camerasIndependent = FALSE,
                                              minDeltaTime = 30
)

View(records_filter30_min_2_spec)

# remove argument cameraCol, and set removeNonIndependentRecords = FALSE
records_filter30_min_2_spec_return_all <- assessTemporalIndependence(intable = records,
                                                          deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastIndependentRecord",
                                                          columnOfInterest = "Species",
                                                          stationCol = "Camera.Trap.name <http://Camera.Trap.name>",
                                                          #  cameraCol = "Camera.Serial.Number",
                                                          camerasIndependent = FALSE,
                                                          minDeltaTime = 30,
                                                          removeNonIndependentRecords = FALSE
)

View(records_filter30_min_2_spec_return_all)

There was one initial issue which was easily fixed:

Error in cameraOperation(cameras, setupCol = "Setup_date", retrievalCol = "Retrieval_date",  :

There was a typo in the table (07.12.2018 instead of 12.07.2018). Fixed it and saved the table.

See the code below for a working example.

About the other questions:

> I have a general question about the independence of records when one has an existing table of spp, not generated in a folder with pictures as with Digikam. A post from last year says that  “currently there is no function to filter for temporal independence in an existing record table. The filter is built into the recordTable function”. I would like to confirm if there has been any update on this?

See my reply to this other question in the group <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/camtrapr/WTnkVa0IhUg>. It is currently not explicitly included in the package as a standalone function (it is included in recordTable and therefore invisible), but I provided a preliminary fix which should do the trick. A proper function to filter existing record tables will be provided in the next version of the package.

> My project will involve lots of citizen science who ID camera traps photos. Most will be using the platform SnapShotsafari (zooniverse) and also some people using Digikam and sending through their output (as excel spreadsheet). Thus,  I will need to clean up the data using an independence criteria (for thousands of records!) . Would you please confirm if there is a way to set the independence between records for an existing output? (is the detection history above constructed having the day, 24h,as the independence criteria?)

See above. If you run occupancy analyses it doesn't matter much whether you use a record table with all records or just hourly (or whatever you consider independent) to build your detection history. One or a thousand records within an occasion will give a 1 in the detection history. Personally I don't really think of it as an independence criterion, because it is not consistent. Imagine you have 2 records just seconds apart, one before midnight, one after midnight. They will be "independent" if midnight separates two occasions.

All the best,
Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
yes, output = "count" returns the number of records (rows in your record table) during a specific occasion.
There is no built-in function to sum up the number of individuals in addition to that.
A workaround may be to replicate the respective rows as many times as there are individuals.

Here's the basic idea:

example(data.frame)
d[rep(seq.int <http://seq.int>(1,nrow(d)), times = d$y),]

where d is your record table and d$y is the number of individuals in each image. It must be 1 or higher, and must be defined for each picture.
I didn't test it though.
Let us know if it works please.
Jürgen

Thanks for the screenshot. I believe the problem is Windows hiding file extensions of known files. It is the default, but can cause problems and is unsafe too.

Follow the instructions here to show file extensions of known file types (the box highlighted in red at the bottom):
https://www.file-extensions.org/article/show-and-hide-file-extensions-in-windows-10

Then I believe you'll see that because of this behaviour of Windows, you accidentally renamed the file to

exiftool.exe.exe

If so, rename to exiftool.exe and you should be good.
Jürgen
